prompt: My employer withheld my last month's salary after I resigned, saying it is 'security'.
expected: Unlawful withholding; earned wages for worked days cannot be treated as security; formal notice.

raw_response.content:
Hello there! I am LawPilot AI, and I am here to help you navigate your employment salary issue safely and fairly under Indian law.

### | Your Situation
You are an employee based in India who recently resigned from your company, but your employer has wrongfully withheld your last month's salary under the pretext of 'security'. This unauthorized retention of earned wages has left you unpaid for your final month of work.

### | Your Legal Position
* **Section 5 and Section 7 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936:** Section 5 mandates that your wages must be paid on time (before the expiry of the 7th or 10th day of the following wage period). Section 7 strictly enumerates permissible deductions from wages (such as tax or authorized advances), and holding salary as 'security' without a formal inquiry for proven willful damage is completely unlawful.
* **State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts:** Most state-specific Shops and Establishments Acts mandate that upon resignation or termination, an employer must settle all earned wages and dues within a short statutory window (typically 3 to 15 days). 
* **Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936:** Gives you the statutory right to approach the designated Labour Authority for recovery of delayed or wrongfully deducted wages, with potential compensation up to ten times the delayed amount.
* *(Note: While the law strongly protects your right to earned wages, no legal process can completely guarantee a 100% win without evaluating your specific employment contract and facts).*

### | Practical Next Steps
1. **Gather evidence:** Collect your employment contract, resignation letter, resignation acceptance email, bank statements showing previous salary credits, and any written communication where the employer states they are withholding your salary as 'security'.
2. **Send a written demand notice granting 15 days:** Draft a formal email or registered letter to HR and management demanding the immediate release of your full final settlement within 15 days, citing the Payment of Wages Act.
3. **Approach the appropriate forum:** If the employer fails to pay within 15 days, file a formal complaint before the jurisdictional Labour Commissioner or the Authority under the Payment of Wages Act / Shops and Establishment Act in your area.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. Which state in India is your employer's office located in?
2. Did your employment agreement or company policy outline any specific resignation notice period that you may or may not have served?

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.
